key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide metal-ceramic coatings can have their roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity tuned by adjusting process parameters, with optimal settings yielding maximum water repellency.
engineering_relevance: This work provides practical parameter–property relationships for selecting detonation spraying conditions that improve coating surface performance in wear- and corrosion-sensitive applications.
method: Varied detonation spraying process conditions, especially nozzle passage speed and spray distance.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle to assess hydrophobicity.
Derived empirical laws linking roughness/thickness to speed and roughness/contact angle to spray distance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental dependence of surface properties on process parameters and states that new equations were obtained for predicting coating characteristics and identifying the optimal spraying mode.
watch_item: The reported relationships are empirical and likely specific to the studied material system and process window, so transfer to other powders, substrates, or spray setups may require recalibration.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
